slides.say: n is a positive odd number. The product n, times n plus two, times n plus four, is necessarily divisible by:

So n is positive and odd. n, n plus two and n plus four are three odd numbers in a row, and we multiply them. What number is the product always divisible by? [short pause] We'll start with one group and check the choices. If several choices remain, we'll choose another group that helps separate them. Then we'll explain why the answer always works.
at: three odd numbers in a row

slides.say: [short pause] Start with the smallest group, one, three and five. One times three times five is fifteen. Fifteen is not divisible by forty-five, so choice number one is out.
But fifteen does divide by fifteen, five and three. So all three of those choices still work for this example. We need another group to tell them apart.

Let's test whether the product must divide by five. Choose three odd numbers in a row that do not include a multiple of five: seven, nine and eleven. Seven times nine is sixty-three, and sixty-three times eleven is six hundred ninety-three.

Six hundred ninety-three ends in three, so it does not divide by five. That also means it does not divide by fifteen. Choice numbers two and four are out. Only three is left, and choice number three is our answer.

Now careful with your choice of numbers. Three times five times seven is a hundred five. Five times seven times nine is three hundred fifteen. Both divide by fifteen because they include a five in the multiplication. They would not rule out fifteen. That's why we chose seven, nine and eleven for the second test.

[pause] Why does the product always divide by three? Look at the odd multiples of three: three, nine, fifteen and twenty-one. They appear once in every three odd numbers. So any three odd numbers in a row include a multiple of three.

Seven, nine and eleven include nine. Eleven, thirteen and fifteen include fifteen. So one number in the multiplication divides by three, and the whole product divides by three too. Choice number three is our answer. Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
